assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Alpha particle
items.clue: A helium nucleus: two protons and two neutrons.

items.label: Mass defect
items.clue: How much lighter a nucleus is than its separated nucleons.

items.label: Activity
items.clue: The number of nuclei in a sample that decay per unit time.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results of the Geiger–Marsden–Rutherford alpha-particle scattering experiment is correct?

options.text: Most of the alpha particles were deflected through large angles, and only a few passed straight through.
Nearly all the alpha particles passed through almost undeflected; a very few were deflected by more than 90°.
The few alpha particles that bounced back had collided with the electrons in the gold atoms.
The few alpha particles that bounced back had struck the hard outer surface of a gold nucleus.

questions.stem: Chlorine-35 and chlorine-37 are two isotopes of chlorine. A chlorine-35 nucleus contains 17 protons. Which statement about a chlorine-37 nucleus is correct?

options.text: It contains 17 protons and 20 neutrons.
It contains 19 protons and 18 neutrons.
It contains 17 protons and 18 neutrons.
It contains 17 protons and 37 neutrons.

questions.explanation: Isotopes of one element have the same proton number, so chlorine-37 also has 17 protons. The nucleon number counts protons and neutrons together: chlorine-35 has 35 − 17 = 18 neutrons and chlorine-37 has 37 − 17 = 20, two more.

questions.stem: White light, containing all visible wavelengths, passes through a cool gas of a single element and is then examined with a spectrometer. What is observed?

options.text: Dark lines at wavelengths that differ from all of the element's emission lines.
Dark lines at wavelengths that match some of the element's emission lines.
A dark band across every wavelength shorter than the one for the smallest energy gap.
A complete spectrum with no dark lines, as the atoms re-emit all the light they absorb.

questions.stem: An atom has energy levels at −10.0 eV (the ground state), −5.0 eV and −3.0 eV. An atom in its ground state is struck by a photon of energy 3.0 eV. What happens?

options.text: The photon is absorbed, and the electron moves up to the −3.0 eV energy level.
The photon is not absorbed, as it matches neither gap from the ground state, 15.0 or 13.0 eV.
The photon is not absorbed, as it matches neither gap from the ground state, 5.0 or 7.0 eV.
The photon is absorbed, and the electron moves up to an energy of −7.0 eV.

questions.explanation: From the ground state a photon can be absorbed only if its energy exactly equals an upward gap, (−5.0) − (−10.0) = 5.0 eV or (−3.0) − (−10.0) = 7.0 eV, or if it is at least 10.0 eV, enough to ionize the atom. 3.0 eV is neither, so the photon is not absorbed and passes on.

questions.stem: In a sodium atom, an electron makes a transition from an energy level at −3.03 eV to one at −5.14 eV. What is the frequency of the emitted photon? Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and 1 eV = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J.

The spectrum of light from a star shows strong dark lines at exactly the wavelengths of the two bright yellow lines in the laboratory emission spectrum of sodium. What can be concluded from this evidence?

options.text: Sodium is absent from the star, because the light at sodium's wavelengths is missing from its spectrum.
Nothing about sodium, because an element absorbs at different wavelengths from those it emits.
Sodium is the most abundant element in the star, because its absorption lines are so strong.
Sodium atoms in the star's outer layers absorb light at these wavelengths, so sodium is present in the star.

questions.stem: Which pair are isotopes of the same element?

options.text: ⁴⁰₁₈Ar and ⁴⁰₁₉K
³¹₁₅P and ³²₁₆S
²³₁₁Na and ²³₁₁Na⁺
³⁵₁₇Cl and ³⁷₁₇Cl

questions.explanation: Both nuclides have proton number Z = 17, so both are chlorine. They differ in nucleon number (35 and 37), so chlorine-35 has 18 neutrons and chlorine-37 has 20: the same element, different numbers of neutrons, which is what isotopes are.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the binding energy of a nucleus?

options.text: The energy released when the nucleus is separated completely into its nucleons.
The energy stored inside the nucleus, which it gives out when it later decays.
The minimum energy needed to pull the nucleus apart into separate nucleons.
The energy equivalent of the extra mass a nucleus has over its separate nucleons.

questions.explanation: Nucleons attract one another through the strong nuclear force, so energy must be supplied to pull them apart. The binding energy is this energy; it equals the mass defect multiplied by c².

questions.stem: Approximate binding energies per nucleon are: ²₁H 1.1 MeV; ⁴₂He 7.1 MeV; ²⁸₁₄Si 8.4 MeV; ⁵⁶₂₆Fe 8.8 MeV; ¹¹⁸₄₆Pd 8.5 MeV; ²³⁶₉₂U 7.6 MeV. Which of these processes would release energy?

options.text: Splitting one ⁵⁶₂₆Fe nucleus into two ²⁸₁₄Si nuclei
Joining two ¹¹⁸₄₆Pd nuclei into one ²³⁶₉₂U nucleus
Separating one ⁴₂He nucleus into its four free nucleons
Fusing two ²₁H nuclei to form one ⁴₂He nucleus

questions.explanation: Both deuterium nuclei move far up the binding energy curve: the total binding energy rises from 2 × 2 × 1.1 = 4.4 MeV to 4 × 7.1 = 28.4 MeV, so about 24 MeV is released.

questions.stem: What did Rutherford conclude about the structure of the atom from the results of the Geiger–Marsden experiment?

options.text: Its nucleus consists of protons and neutrons, which the experiment first detected.
It is a solid ball, and most alpha particles passed through the gaps between the atoms.
Its positive charge and nearly all its mass are in a tiny central nucleus.
Its electrons are heavy enough to turn back any alpha particles that hit them.

questions.explanation: Only a small, massive, concentrated positive charge can repel an alpha particle strongly enough to turn it back, and the fact that so few were turned back shows that this nucleus fills only a tiny fraction of the atom.

questions.stem: A nucleus of potassium-40 is written in nuclear notation as ⁴⁰₁₉K. Which statement about this nucleus is correct?

options.text: It contains 40 neutrons.
It contains 19 neutrons.
It contains 19 nucleons.
It contains 21 neutrons.

questions.explanation: In ᴬ_Z X the upper number is the nucleon number A = 40 and the lower number is the proton number Z = 19, so the number of neutrons is N = A − Z = 40 − 19 = 21.

questions.stem: The emission spectrum of a hot, low-pressure gas of one element consists of bright lines at a set of separate wavelengths. Why is this evidence that the atoms have discrete energy levels?

options.text: Each line has the photon energy of one allowed level, so each line marks one energy level.
The lines are equally spaced in frequency, just as the atom's energy levels are equally spaced.
Each line is emitted as an electron jumps up from one allowed level to a higher level.
Each line has a single photon energy, equal to the difference between two of the atom's allowed energies.

questions.stem: A flat loop of wire is placed in a uniform magnetic field. In which situation is the magnetic flux through the loop zero?

options.text: Its plane is perpendicular to the field lines, so θ in Φ = BA cos θ is 90°.
It is held at rest in the field, so the field through it is not changing.
Its plane is parallel to the field lines, so no field lines pass through the loop.
At no orientation: while a loop is inside a field, flux must pass through it.

questions.explanation: Φ = BA cos θ, with θ measured from the normal. When the plane of the loop is parallel to the field, the normal is perpendicular to it, θ = 90° and cos θ = 0, so Φ = 0: the field lines run alongside the loop and none pass through it.

questions.stem: A flat rectangular coil of 100 turns measures 4.0 cm by 5.0 cm. It starts with its plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of strength 0.40 T and is then rotated through 60° in 0.050 s, about an axis perpendicular to the field. What is the magnitude of the average emf induced during the rotation?
questions.explanation: At the start θ = 0° (field along the normal), so Φ₁ = BA. After turning 60°, θ = 60°, so Φ₂ = BA cos 60° = 0.5BA. ΔΦ = 0.5 × 0.40 × 2.0 × 10⁻³ = 4.0 × 10⁻⁴ Wb. ε = NΔΦ/Δt = 100 × 4.0 × 10⁻⁴ / 0.050 = 0.80 V.

questions.stem: A flat square coil of 100 turns and side 5.0 cm moves at a constant 0.60 m s⁻¹ into a region of uniform magnetic field of strength 0.20 T. The plane of the coil is perpendicular to the field and its leading side is parallel to the edge of the field region. What is the emf induced in the coil while it is entering the field?

A strong bar magnet is released from rest and falls vertically down the centre of a long vertical copper tube. How does its fall compare with a fall from rest through the same height in air outside the tube?

options.text: It falls more slowly, because currents induced in the tube exert forces that oppose its motion.
It falls in the same way, because copper is not magnetic and so exerts no force on it.
It falls faster, because the currents induced in the tube pull it downwards.
It is pulled sideways onto the wall and sticks there, as a magnet attracts metals.

questions.stem: A rectangular coil of 40 turns measures 6.0 cm by 4.0 cm. It rotates at a constant 25 revolutions per second about an axis through its centre, parallel to its 6.0 cm sides and perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of strength 0.10 T. What is the peak emf induced in the coil?
questions.explanation: Each 6.0 cm side is 0.020 m from the axis, so it moves at v = 2πfr = 2π × 25 × 0.020 = 3.14 m s⁻¹. When the plane is parallel to the field both sides move perpendicular to it, each with emf BvL, and these add around the loop: ε = 2NBvL = 2 × 40 × 0.10 × 3.14 × 0.060 = 1.5 V.

questions.stem: A rectangular coil rotates at a constant frequency in a uniform magnetic field. A graph of the induced emf against time is a sine curve that is zero at t = 0, 10 ms, 20 ms, 30 ms and 40 ms, with maxima of +4.0 V at 5 ms and 25 ms and minima of −4.0 V at 15 ms and 35 ms. The coil is then made to rotate at 40 revolutions per second in the same field. What is the new peak emf?
questions.explanation: The period is the time from one maximum to the next, 25 ms − 5 ms = 20 ms, so the original frequency is 50 Hz. The peak emf is proportional to the rotation frequency: 4.0 V × 40/50 = 3.2 V.
